internal static class BuilderRpcWireMapper
{
    internal static BuilderRpcRequest ToDomain(BuilderExecuteRequest request)
        => new(
            request.Kind switch
            {
                BuilderOperation.ListWorkspaces => BuilderRpcOperationKind.ListWorkspaces,
                BuilderOperation.ResolveWorkspace => BuilderRpcOperationKind.ResolveWorkspace,
                BuilderOperation.ExecuteProcess => BuilderRpcOperationKind.ExecuteProcess,
                BuilderOperation.ExecuteShell => BuilderRpcOperationKind.ExecuteShell,
                BuilderOperation.MapToHostPath => BuilderRpcOperationKind.MapToHostPath,
                BuilderOperation.AddPathEntry => BuilderRpcOperationKind.AddPathEntry,
                _ => throw new InvalidDataException("The Builder RPC operation is invalid."),
            },
            request.WorkspaceId,
            request.FileName,
            request.Arguments,
            request.Command,
            request.WorkingDirectory,
            checked((int)request.TimeoutSeconds),
            request.ExecutionPath);

    internal static BuilderExecuteRequest ToWire(BuilderRpcRequest request)
        => new()
        {
            Kind = request.Kind switch
            {
                BuilderRpcOperationKind.ListWorkspaces => BuilderOperation.ListWorkspaces,
                BuilderRpcOperationKind.ResolveWorkspace => BuilderOperation.ResolveWorkspace,
                BuilderRpcOperationKind.ExecuteProcess => BuilderOperation.ExecuteProcess,
                BuilderRpcOperationKind.ExecuteShell => BuilderOperation.ExecuteShell,
                BuilderRpcOperationKind.MapToHostPath => BuilderOperation.MapToHostPath,
                BuilderRpcOperationKind.AddPathEntry => BuilderOperation.AddPathEntry,
                _ => throw new InvalidDataException("The Builder RPC operation is invalid."),
            },
            WorkspaceId = request.WorkspaceId,
            FileName = request.FileName,
            Arguments = request.Arguments,
            Command = request.Command,
            WorkingDirectory = request.WorkingDirectory,
            TimeoutSeconds = request.TimeoutSeconds,
            ExecutionPath = request.ExecutionPath,
        };
}

# Sunder Package Agent Protocol

> **Migration-only project:** this project preserves the current descriptor and
> ABI corpus until implementation-first generation proves canonical parity. It is
> deleted before final V1 release and is not a future public package boundary.

Schema-first RPC descriptors and deterministic C# bindings for packages that integrate with the `sunder.package.agent` 2.x family.

```xml
<PackageReference Include="Sunder.Package.Agent.Protocol" Version="[2.0.0,3.0.0)" />
```

Runtime extensions must also declare a `sunder.package.agent` dependency with `>=2.0.0 <3.0.0`. Worker V1 targets pass immutable `SunderWorkerProviderRegistration` entries in `SunderWorkerOptions` to `SunderWorker.RunAsync`. The Host validates every request, response, and stream event against the bundled contract descriptor.

This project's historical source directory and some public namespaces use `Sunder.Package.Agent.Contracts`. The built assembly, NuGet package, embedded descriptor resource prefix, and generated binding namespaces use `Sunder.Package.Agent.Protocol`. The retained source names are implementation/API organization within this one artifact; they do not represent another package or shared cross-package CLR types.

The package contains exactly 19 checked-in descriptors and generates deterministic DTO/client/provider sources during the build. Its `buildTransitive` assets bundle those descriptors into each consuming Sunder package.

V1 scalar semantics are explicit: identifiers use the `uuid` logical type, UTC timestamps use `utc-date-time`, and numeric model options and embedding components use binary64-compatible JSON numbers. Generated timestamp bindings retain canonical text with one through nine fractional digits; handwritten adapters accept the same range and project it to `DateTimeOffset` tick precision where their public contracts require it.

`Microsoft.Extensions.AI.ChatOptions` exposes temperature, top-p, frequency-penalty, and presence-penalty values as binary32 fields. Agent RPC carries their lossless binary64 widenings. A schema-first caller must therefore send a finite binary64 value that is exactly the widening of a binary32 value; the chat and run-control adapters fail with `agent.chat.option-not-representable` instead of rounding any other schema-valid value.
